statement: Combined capex of the 5 largest spenders falls year on year for 2 consecutive quarters (securities filings; by 2028-06-30)
status_at_phase_end: Far from triggering: combined quarterly capex of the four largest Bloc A cloud/platform spenders rose every quarter of 2026 (~$130B Q1, ~$165B Q2, ~$202-209B Q3), +84-108% year over year in Q3; all guide to higher 2027 spending. Fifth-largest spender varies by basis (an enterprise-cloud provider, ~$28.5B in its latest quarter, or a space/AI conglomerate). Stress signal: free cash flow turned negative at several, funded by record bond issuance.

items.summary: Q1 2026 combined capex of the four largest Bloc A hyperscalers ~$129.8B, up ~80% year over year from ~$71.9B.
items.detail: Purchases of property and equipment, three months (Microsoft: additions to property and equipment), $B: Microsoft 30.9, Alphabet 35.7, Amazon 44.2, Meta 19.0; total 129.8 (year earlier 71.9). Read from each company's quarterly earnings release (investor-relations copy; same cash-flow line as the 10-Q): https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-Reports-First-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx, https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-release/news-release-details/2026/Amazon-com-Announces-First-Quarter-Results/default.aspx, https://s206.q4cdn.com/479360582/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/2026q1-alphabet-earnings-release.pdf, https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/earnings/FY-2026-Q3/cash-flows. Combined value public on 2026-04-29 (last of the four releases).

items.summary: Q2 2026 combined capex of the same four firms ~$165.1B, up ~87% year over year.
items.detail: Purchases of property and equipment, three months (Microsoft: additions to property and equipment), $B: Microsoft 35.8, Alphabet 44.9, Amazon 54.2, Meta 30.1; total 165.1 (year earlier 88.2). Read from each company's quarterly earnings release (investor-relations copy; same cash-flow line as the 10-Q): https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx, https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-release/news-release-details/2026/Amazon-com-Announces-Second-Quarter-Results/default.aspx, https://s206.q4cdn.com/479360582/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/2026q2-alphabet-earnings-release.pdf, https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/earnings/FY-2026-Q4/press-release-webcast. Combined value public on 2026-07-30 (last of the four releases). (An earlier version also said one firm raised its full-year range in July; that clause was dropped because the guidance source could not be opened.)

items.summary: Q3 2026: the four largest spenders reported ~$207B of capex, up about 85% year on year; none cut its 2026 capex range (combined guidance $720-740B).
items.detail: Amazon 77.3 (cash capex 75.9), Alphabet 51.4, Microsoft 39.4 (45.2 incl. finance leases), Meta 33.9-34.9, Oracle 28.5 (FY27Q1). Earnings 2026-10-21 (Meta), 10-28 (Alphabet, Microsoft), 10-29 (Amazon).

items.summary: All four largest spenders signalled higher 2027 capex ('increase significantly', 'meaningfully more', 'accelerate', 'continue investing aggressively'); implied Q4 2026 combined capex (incl. a fifth firm) $247-272B.
items.detail: Q3 2026 earnings calls (Alphabet CFO Ashkenazi; Amazon CFO Olsavsky; Microsoft; Meta). Business Insider tally incl. SpaceX: $556B spent in first three quarters, $803-828B full-year.

items.summary: Financing strain: in Q3 2026 capex exceeded operating cash flow at four of the five largest spenders (combined shortfall ~$32B); one raised $115B of long-term debt in nine months. A leading indicator of possible future cuts, not yet a decline.
items.detail: Alphabet FCF -$9.1B, Meta -$1.2 to -2.1B, Oracle -$5.4B, Amazon -$34.8B (quarter), Microsoft +$18.6B. Kufenberg / Global Terminal from filings.
